value.rationale: Connected half-graphs are canonical finite order-property and instability witnesses in finite graph model theory. The result completely describes their rank-four graph-language logical quotient, gives the natural sharp fourteen-point kernel, and isolates a nontrivial difference between the uncoloured boundary \(H_7\)/\(H_8\) and the side-labelled \(H_7\)/\(H_8\). It requires a genuine composition argument across arbitrary graph orders and exact type checking at a sharp boundary, not a textbook renaming or arbitrary isolated small case. The exact finite logical invariant is useful for studying elementary visibility of the standard unstable-pattern family, independently of a larger theorem.
